name: MEI Industrial Solutions Providence
old_description: Formerly known as Accurate Metal Sales & Fabrication, MEI provides retail metal sales and custom metal fabrication, sub-assemblies and weldments to the general public as well as the commercial construction industry, municipalities and residential general contractors. Our capabilities include 3D engineered drawings, design renderings, manufacturing, structural repairs, complex weldments, rigging and installation of finished product. All our welders are AWS D1.1 structural certified as well as MIL certified for military and defense contracts. We use advanced tools such as CNC plasma cutting to fabricate high quality weldments to meet our client’s exact requirements and delivery deadlines.
about:
MEI Industrial Solutions operates from Southbridge, Massachusetts, where it runs a fabrication facility and retail metal yard on Ashland Avenue. The business was formerly known as Accurate Metal Sales & Fabrication before adopting its current name.

The company provides custom metal fabrication, including sub-assemblies, weldments, structural repairs, and complex weldments, along with rigging and installation of finished products. Its shop is equipped with a high-definition plasma table cutting up to 1.5-inch mild steel, hydraulic shear, vertical band saw, radial arm drill, press brake, roll forming equipment, an ironworker, and multiple MIG, TIG, and stick welding machines. In-house design services use SolidWorks and AutoCAD to produce conceptual and engineered blueprints, and the staff performs cutting, drilling, grinding, beveling, oxyacetylene and plasma torch cutting, jigging, fit-up, and assembly.

MEI serves the general public through retail metal sales, as well as commercial construction firms, municipalities, residential general contractors, and military and defense contracts. Its inventory includes a wide range of structural steel shapes, plate, tubing, and pipe in standard sizes.

The company emphasizes that all its welders hold AWS D1.1 structural certification and MIL certification for defense work, and it uses CNC plasma cutting to meet exact requirements and delivery deadlines. On-site fabrication and installation services are also available.

name: MGM Transformers (a Forgent company)
old_description: Dry-type and liquid-filled distribution/power transformers (cast coil, VPI, padmount)
about:
MGM Transformers, headquartered in Vernon, California, traces its origins to 1926 and has operated under the MGM name since 1974. Now a subsidiary of Forgent, the company designs and manufactures transformers for power distribution across North America.

The company produces dry-type transformers — including vacuum pressure impregnated (VPI) and cast coil designs — as well as liquid-filled padmount and substation units. It also builds custom power distribution unit (PDU) transformers for high-density data centers and general-purpose low-voltage transformers. Manufacturing is vertically integrated across five facilities totaling 1.5 million square feet in California, Texas, and Tijuana, Mexico, with a workforce of approximately 1,500 employees.

MGM serves data center operators (from hyperscale to edge), solar and renewable energy developers, commercial and industrial facilities, utilities, and industrial manufacturing plants. Its transformers are specified for grid modernization projects, including utility-scale solar, storage, and substation infrastructure. A noted example is Standard Solar, which received a grounding transformer in four weeks to restore site operations.

The company emphasizes vertically integrated manufacturing, lead times, and a rush-order program (Bull Rush) for urgent needs. It stocks transformers in 20 major U.S. cities for rapid deployment and reports a 98% on-time delivery rate across a $4 billion installed base.

name: MMR Group, Inc.
old_description: MMR Group consistently ranks at the top of Engineering News-Record's annual specialty contractors list. We're no stranger to 1 million work-hour projects, and we manage 30 offices throughout North and South America.
about:
MMR Group, Inc. is headquartered in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and operates 30 offices throughout North and South America. The company’s founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, but it has grown into a specialty contractor consistently ranked at the top of Engineering News-Record’s annual list.

The firm provides electrical construction, instrumentation, power distribution, panel and modular control building fabrication, telecommunications and security systems, commissioning and start-up, power development, maintenance, mission critical construction, and power engineering and utility services. It self-performs electrical, telecommunications, security, fire alarm, and gas services, and recently opened a Modular Systems facility in Lafayette, Louisiana, to assemble and test data center skids off-site. With approximately 725 employees, MMR routinely manages projects exceeding one million work-hours.

MMR serves the chemical and petrochemical, oil and gas (upstream, midstream, downstream), industrial manufacturing, power generation, renewable energy and energy storage, and telecommunications sectors. Project references include the Black Hills Energy Cheyenne Prairie Power Project (Wyoming), Kinder Morgan Elba Island 35kV/15kV project (Georgia), Shell Canada Albian Oil Sands Expansion (Alberta), Procter & Gamble tissue machine plant (Missouri), GE/Entergy Perryville energy storage system (Louisiana), and Chevron’s Big Foot production platform (Gulf of Mexico).

The company attributes its differentiation to diverse expertise across broad sectors, a commitment to safety and quality, state-of-the-art project controls, cutting-edge technology, and a workforce of certified craftsmen. It emphasizes completing projects on schedule and within budget since inception.

name: MRL Equipment Company
old_description: MRL Equipment Co. Inc. has manufactured pavement marking, removal, grooving, and pavement maintenance equipment for over 36 years. Founded by road stripers with first-hand knowledge and background in striping and removal operations, MRL innovates with the customer to produce customized paint, thermoplastic, plural component, line removal/pavement grooving, water blasting, bituminous marking equipment and more.
about:
MRL Equipment Company operates from Billings, Montana, where it has built pavement marking, removal, grooving, and pavement maintenance equipment for more than three decades. The business was started by road stripers who brought first-hand experience from striping and removal operations, shaping a company that designs machinery around the practical needs of the people who use it daily.

The company produces a range of specialized trucks and systems, including thermoplastic applicators with 12,000‑lb and 16,000‑lb capacity, the EpoxyPro plural‑component impingement mixing system, removal and grooving trucks that use a multiple‑head progressive removal system to limit surface damage, and road marking and raised‑pavement‑marker equipment designed for high‑volume output and ease of service. MRL also offers retrofit kits, parts support, and financing options to keep fleets running.

Primary customers are pavement marking contractors, state and municipal highway departments, and striping crews who need reliable, high‑throughput equipment for line removal, groove cutting, water blasting, and bituminous marking applications. The company’s "built by stripers, for stripers" philosophy means each machine is developed with direct input from the operators who will run it.

MRL says its differentiation comes from designing equipment in collaboration with end users, resulting in features such as heated delivery systems that reduce downtime and a progressive removal head that balances speed with surface preservation. The focus on customization and operator‑centric design traces back to the founders’ own backgrounds in the trade.

name: Mace MFG
old_description: In 2023, I took a leap of faith and founded Mace Manufacturing. My tinkering on nights and weekends began with 3D printers and CNC routers. This eventually evolved into acquiring a CNC plasma table to design and fabricate a replacement floor for my 1974 Toyota Land Cruiser. As most of you know, as we get older, our tools just get bigger and more expensive. In February of 2023, I decided to sell my dream car, which was a 1993 Nissan Skyline GTR, to purchase a HAAS VF2 and challenge myself to develop unique and innovative automotive machined accessories.
about:
Mace MFG is based in Indian Land, South Carolina. Founded in 2023 by Stuart, a mechanical engineer, the company began as a nights-and-weekends project using 3D printers and CNC routers. After fabricating a replacement floor for a 1974 Toyota Land Cruiser with a CNC plasma table, Stuart sold a 1993 Nissan Skyline GT-R in February 2023 to purchase a HAAS VF2 vertical machining center, committing full-time to producing machined automotive accessories.

The shop focuses on precision-machined accessories for off-road Toyota and Lexus vehicles. Using the HAAS VF2 alongside 3D printing and CNC plasma cutting, Mace MFG produces billet aluminum volume knobs (marketed as "Knobbies"), titanium-and-Ultem key fob cases, battery tie-downs, shift knobs, front bump stops, rail T-nuts, and battery clamp J-hooks. Materials include 6061 aluminum, titanium, Ultem (PEI), and polycarbonate. The product line spans multiple SKUs across 4Runner, Tundra, Tacoma, Sequoia, GX, LX, and FJ Cruiser models.

The company serves the automotive aftermarket, specifically off-road and overlanding enthusiasts driving Toyota and Lexus trucks and SUVs. Customers purchase directly through the Mace MFG web store; notable community figures such as Keith Charvonia of Charvonia Design, Patrick Perry of Perry Parts, and Colten Johnson of Teton Workshop are featured as collaborators.

Mace MFG emphasizes American manufacturing and engineering-driven design, stating that every detail is scrutinized to deliver quality without compromise. The founder's background in automotive design and manufacturing informs a philosophy of "innovation drives us" and "from our hands to yours."

name: Machined In Wood
old_description: Machined In Wood is a custom CNC woodworking shop that specializes in CNC machined wood projects, laser engraving, and finishing of custom one of a kind pieces, prototypes, and small to medium scale manufacturing.
about:
Machined In Wood operates from Bellingham, Massachusetts. The shop began as a home-based business and has expanded to serve both individual clients and commercial manufacturers.

The company provides custom CNC woodworking services including V-carving, 3D carving, precision machined parts, and profile cuts in sheet goods. It also offers laser cutting and engraving with CO2 and diode lasers, 3D printing for prototyping, traditional woodworking (table saw, band saw, jointer, planer, drum sander, router, sanding), and painting and finishing such as hand painting, airbrushing, HVLP spraying, stains, clear coats, and food-grade finishes. Two 48" x 48" CNC routers (one with pass-through capability) and a horizontal boring machine support production runs from dozens to hundreds of parts.

Customers range from individual hobbyists and makers to other wood shops and commercial firms. The shop works with engineers and designers on production parts, accepting customer-supplied material and collaborating via blueprints, CAD models, and GD&T specifications. Projects include one-of-a-kind pieces, prototypes, and small-to-medium scale manufacturing for clients across the United States.

Machined In Wood differentiates itself with equipment that many small shops do not invest in, notably a horizontal boring machine for precise horizontal holes and the ability to flatten material up to 48" x 48" on its CNC routers. The company emphasizes proficiency with technical drawings and GD&T, maintains a 1% tolerance level, and conducts rigorous QA inspections. It also takes on smaller projects that larger shops often decline.

name: Mack Molding Co
old_description: Mack Molding specializes in custom injection molding, providing high-quality plastic components tailored to diverse industry needs.
about:
Mack Molding Co. was founded in 1920 and operates as a vertically integrated contract manufacturer headquartered in Arlington, Vermont, with a southern division in Inman, South Carolina. The company began as a custom injection molding specialist and has expanded over more than a century into a multi-facility operation.

Today Mack Molding provides end-to-end manufacturing services including plastic injection molding (120+ presses ranging from 28 to 4,000 tons, shot sizes of 0.6 to 769 ounces), large-part molding, Class A painting, CNC machining, sheet metal fabrication, assembly, and supply chain management. The company runs ten facilities totaling more than 1.5 million square feet of manufacturing space and supports production volumes from prototype quantities of five pieces up to five million units annually.

Its customer base spans medical device, industrial equipment, transportation, robotics, energy and utilities, and defense sectors, serving both publicly traded Fortune 500 companies and private enterprises. The firm is FDA and ITAR registered, enabling work on regulated medical products and defense programs.

Mack Molding emphasizes a “one partner, total responsibility” model, positioning itself as an extension of the client’s manufacturing team. It highlights financial stability (debt‑free with a 5A1 Dun & Bradstreet rating), deep in‑house engineering and tooling capabilities, and a vertically integrated approach designed to reduce lead times, coordinate multi‑material production, and maintain consistent quality across complex programs.
